official_sources: HMLR Practice Guide 5 adverse possession unregistered land
official_measurement_examples: HMLR first-registration guidance was updated 16 June 2026
an unsuccessful online registered-title search does not prove land has no owner
first registration records an existing legal estate rather than creating development permission
root-of-title and deed evidence remain central for unregistered land
lost deeds require a separate evidence and title-quality assessment
index-map search can help determine whether land is registered but is not itself ownership proof
unregistered/first-registration status does not establish planning permission access rights or final development yield
core_rules: unregistered land is not ownerless land
no online title result is not no owner
first registration is not planning permission
first registration is not automatic proof of every historic right
root of title must be evidenced
lost deeds require special evidence route
index-map result is not title deed
land-charge search remains distinct from title register
adverse possession route is distinct from ordinary first registration
registration does not establish access rights beyond title evidence
registration does not prove utility capacity
registration does not discharge restrictive covenants/easements
registration does not calculate development yield
no parcel title clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official HM Land Registry, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked 2026-07-26. June/20 July 2026 first-registration, lost-deeds and index-map guidance currentity retained; no parcel promotion.
